newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, Sept surges to new high.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, Sept surges to new high.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Monday in an active session, with spot-September driven up six percent to a new contract high on strong technical and fund buying after Friday's breakout.

September surged 13.5 cents to close at $2.374 per million British thermal units after earlier hitting a new high of $2.385. October settled 12.3 cents higher at $2.368. Other deferreds ended mixed, with some 1999s down slightly.
"Cash didn't do that much - it was up a couple of cents - but there were tons of short covering today," said one East Coast trader, noting funds jumped in and also helped propel the complex higher.

While growing concerns about storage and some heat in the West could help support physical prices near-term, some doubt current paper levels can be sustained, with cash, for the first time in many weeks, now lagging the screen by almost a dime.
Some said forecasts for below-normal Midwest and Northeast temperatures this week also were not very supportive though a slight warming trend was predicted by the weekend.

And while chart traders agreed September's close Friday above key downtrend resistance turned the technical picture bullish, some said the market was overbought and due for a correction after an 11 percent rally in four sessions.

September support was now pegged at $2.20, then at $2.15-2.16 and along the short-term up trendline in the $2.12 area. Key support was expected at the prominent $2.045 low. Resistance was seen at the new contract high of $2.385, with further selling likely at the May 7 spot continuation high of $2.43.

In the cash Monday, Gulf Coast prices firmed one to two cents to $2.20 or better, with gas at the Hub pegged in the mid-to-high $2.20s. Midcon pipes also were up slightly in the mid-teens. Forecasts for milder New York weather this week pressured city gate prices down modestly to the low-$2.40s.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip jumped another 6.5 cents to $2.324. NYMEX said 75,609 contracts traded, up sharply from Friday's revised tally of 19,658.

On the KCBT, September finished 10.4 cents higher at $2.22, while deferreds ended up by six to 11.6 cents. The East/West spread widened by 3.1 cents to 15.4 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 417 contracts traded, up from Friday's total of 243.
